literal.prompt: Как называется морской лёд в виде округлых дисков с приподнятыми краями?

literalGroups.primaryGround: NSIDC identifies pancake ice as circular disks with raised edges produced when waves bump them (L88); WMO defines pancake ice as predominantly circular pieces 30 cm–3 m in diameter (L30). The competing labels refer to distinct forms or stages: needle-like frazil crystals precede sheets (NSIDC L83-L86), nilas is a thin crust (NSIDC L85; WMO L30), and fast ice is shore/floor attached (WMO L30). The key is unique.
literalGroups.locator: NSIDC turn2view0 L83-L88; WMO turn2view2 L29-L30.

literalGroups.literal: Это блинчатый лёд. Диски формируются и сталкиваются в волнуемой воде, постепенно смерзаясь между собой.
literalGroups.primaryGround: NSIDC states that in rough water frazil crystals accumulate into slushy circular disks called pancakes, and wave collisions create raised edges (L88). It further says the pancakes eventually cement together into a coherent sheet (L91).

literalGroups.literal: Игловидные кристаллы фразиля появляются при начале замерзания морской воды, всплывают и срастаются в ледяной лист.
literalGroups.primaryGround: NSIDC calls the small needle-like ice crystals formed as ocean water begins freezing “frazil”; these crystals float, accumulate and bond into sheets (L84). This supports the note as an earlier stage distinct from pancake disks.

literalGroups.literal: Блинчатый лёд образует преимущественно округлые диски диаметром 30 см–3 м; волны сталкивают их и приподнимают края.
literalGroups.primaryGround: WMO defines pancake ice as predominantly circular pieces 30 cm to 3 m in diameter (L30). NSIDC says waves bump pancake disks together and create raised perimeter edges (L88), grounding both the added size fact and the defining morphology.
literalGroups.locator: WMO turn2view2 L29-L30; NSIDC turn2view0 L88.

literalGroups.literal: Нилас — тонкая упругая сплошная корка морского льда.
literalGroups.primaryGround: NSIDC says grease ice develops into a continuous thin sheet called nilas (L85); WMO characterizes nilas as a thin elastic crust under 10 cm and distinguishes young ice as a later 10–30 cm category (L30). The rewritten note avoids that category mismatch.
literalGroups.locator: NSIDC turn2view0 L85; WMO turn2view2 L30.

literalGroups.literal: Припай — морской лёд, прикреплённый к берегу или дну.
literalGroups.primaryGround: WMO defines fast ice as sea ice attached to the shore or ocean floor (L30), supporting the shorter note “прикреплённый к берегу или дну.”

fourFullPromptAnswerNoteAssessments.grammar: Natural Russian singular definition question; each short answer is a grammatically suitable ice-type label, and every note is a complete readable sentence.
fourFullPromptAnswerNoteAssessments.plausibilityUniqueKeyAndNoteTruthUsefuln: The Russian question is natural and the noun answer labels fit “как называется”. “Ледяные иглы” is a plausible early-formation distractor; nilas is a continuous crust; fast ice is attachment-classified. Only pancake ice matches rounded disks with raised edges. The sources distinguish each form.

correctNoteNewFact.newFact: WMO gives the predominantly circular pancake-ice pieces a diameter range of 30 cm to 3 m.
correctNoteNewFact.whyNew: The prompt gives the round-disk shape and raised edges but no dimensions; the key gives only the category name. This adds an independently useful scale fact about the correct option.

entries.absoluteDifficulty: HARD is appropriate for a general adult audience because identifying “блинчатый лёд” requires specific sea-ice nomenclature: the stem describes a distinct ice form, while related terms such as frazil, nilas and fast ice refer to neighboring but different stages/forms/properties. This is not a broad adult fact.
